title: Majestic… Draw?!: Collect the Pawn Before Racing
summary: Use the king’s capture tempo on the queenside before releasing the distant passed pawn.

nodes.question: White has pushed a6. Which pawn can Black collect immediately?
nodes.explanation: Kc6 attacks b6. Capturing it leaves the a-pawn vulnerable on its next advance. Meanwhile f4 restrains White’s king, and h3 is ready to run once the queenside threats are removed.

branches.title: Independent continuation: collect both pawns, then queen
commentary: Begin in the complete seven-piece diagram after a6 at 106 seconds. The source discusses collecting the pawns, but the exact replies below are independently selected to make the conversion concrete.
Kxb6 removes the nearer passer. It is the only winning move in this exact diagram; racing the h-pawn immediately gives away the win.
a7 advances White’s remaining queenside pawn, but it enters a square attacked by Kb6. This is a representative legal reply, not a forced move.
Kxa7 removes the second passer. Black has eliminated White’s queenside promotion threats before starting the kingside race.
Kxf4 captures Black’s restraining pawn. White has collected material, but moving the king leaves h3 free to advance.
h2 puts the pawn one step from queening. White’s king on f4 cannot reach h1 in a single move.
Kg3 approaches h2 but cannot stop the immediate promotion. This representative defense keeps the exact Black win.
h1=Q promotes. Black’s queen and king win against White’s king and f2 pawn in this exact position; further queen conversion remains to be played.

branches.title: Independent mistake: run before taking b6
commentary: Compare the tempting immediate pawn race while White still has a6 and b6.

h2 changes the exact result to a White win. Black has skipped the essential capture of b6 and left both queenside passers alive. A pawn one step from promotion is not enough to justify ignoring the other wing.

exercises.prompt: Why take b6 before pushing h2?
exercises.answer: Kxb6 is the only winning move in this later position. It removes one passer and puts the king next to the other; the immediate pawn push leaves White a winning queenside race.

exercises.prompt: What does ...Kxa7 change before White takes f4?
exercises.answer: White no longer has either queenside passer. Black can let White spend a king move on f4, then use h2 and h1=Q.
